minutes.headline: Select Board ratified Paul Visconti as the new facilities director and approved a solar PILOT and tax-appeal settlement.
minutes.summary: The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a facilities director, heard the Council on Aging's annual report and a pollinator habitat presentation, and approved the 265 Pleasant Street solar PILOT with a linked settlement of two tax appeal cases. It also discussed the 300th anniversary committee charge, held off approving it until the town manager is back, and began an informal discussion of what to do with 30 School Street after the demolition-only vote at Town Meeting.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to approve the Nugen solar PILOT agreement for 265 Pleasant Street and a settlement ending the two pending tax appeal cases.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of Paul Visconti as facilities director.
The 300th anniversary committee charge was held to the next meeting, to be revised with facilities added and membership capped at 11.
The board discussed 30 School Street after the demolition-only Town Meeting vote and reached no resolution; it will return to the topic in October with a full board.
The board approved a Lions Club toll booth fundraiser and use of the Ritter parking lot on September 24.

why_it_matters: The solar PILOT replaces personal property tax assessments on the 265 Pleasant Street array with a scheduled payment and ends two appeals, which changes what that property pays the town in future years.
30 School Street remains undecided, and members named the cost of the park plan as a barrier to Town Meeting support, so residents may be asked to vote on it again.
watch_next: The municipal building design committee's October update to the board on 30 School Street.
The 300th anniversary committee charge, due back at the next Select Board meeting in revised form.

reconciliation.summary: The three votes match in item and outcome, and the decisions and attendees broadly agree apart from garbled caption names. The substantive differences are the COA volunteer value ($16,800 vs $16,861.32), the unspecified Tricentennial charge revisions, and the park cost figures, which the official minutes leave as 'several million'.
